authorized() at src/remote/mod.rs:144-166 refuses a non-loopback Host with no login (147-149), with a different caller (150-155) and accepts an equal login (153); the three cases at src/remote/mod.rs:782-797 assert exactly those, with the request fixture built at src/remote/mod.rs:761-773. Two corrections to the record: (1) login normalization is at src/remote/mod.rs:79, not 80-85, so the citation is fixed in production_refs/signal_reason; (2) host_is_loopback at src/remote/mod.rs:703-710 returns true for any Host starting with "[::1]" (and splits the port off the rest), so a tailnet peer sending Host: [::1].example is authorized without any login - a real fail-open path adjacent to this gate that neither this row nor the loopback row covers. C=4, U=3 and F=3 stand; S stays 3 because the login comparison is decisively asserted even though the host branch is under-covered.

final_review.behavior: With a configured login, authorized() refuses a non-loopback Host that carries no tailscale-user-login, refuses one carrying a different login, and accepts one carrying the configured login.
final_review.failure_caught: If the non-loopback branch stopped comparing the caller login, any device on the tailnet could read /api/state and POST send, key, kill and transcript to every session - an unauthenticated remote control of terminals and their content.
final_review.criticality_reason: The behaviour is the identity gate on remote access to all sessions: a regression is a privacy breach of transcripts and keystrokes plus a wrong-target control capability, matching the rubric's top band (src/remote/mod.rs:144-166).
final_review.signal_reason: Three cases cover the branch's real shape - missing header, wrong login, right login (src/remote/mod.rs:782-797) - so the login comparison itself is pinned. Missing: the served login is normalized at src/remote/mod.rs:79 (inside serve, 75-82; the record cited 80-85), so a case-varied caller login is untested, and host_is_loopback (src/remote/mod.rs:703-710) accepts any Host that merely starts with "[::1]", so a tailnet request with Host: [::1].example passes the loopback branch with no login at all; no row exercises that spoofed host, and a host without a port is also untested.
final_review.uniqueness_reason: No other test presents a tailscale-user-login header (src/remote/mod.rs:144-166): the only end-to-end suite, tests/remote_web.rs:23-56, binds and calls 127.0.0.1, so the tailnet branch's authority states are protected only by the three gate tests.
final_review.fidelity_reason: The production Gateway::authorized runs, but the tests construct the request struct directly, so the header-parsing layer that produces those names is not in the path (src/remote/mod.rs:761-773).
final_review.recommendation_reason: High-criticality authority assertion with no equivalent coverage elsewhere; it must be retained even though it is a small unit test.
final_review.cost_drivers: 0.018s one hosted attempt; unit test in the ovrcr lib target, no sockets or child processes

findings: authorized() returns false for any non-loopback Host when login is None (src/remote/mod.rs:147-149); the test at src/remote/mod.rs:800-809 asserts loopback still accepted and a tailnet caller carrying a login header still refused. The record's signal_reason already names the same host-parse hole I confirmed in host_is_loopback (src/remote/mod.rs:703-710, the "[::1]" prefix test) plus the missing IPv6/port variants, so S=3 is honest. C=4 (fail-closed default in front of read/keystroke APIs), U=3 (distinct branch from the configured-login row), F=3 (hand-built Request) all stand.

Verified read_request at src/remote/http.rs:139-210 stores header names lowercased (src/remote/http.rs:167) and Request::header compares case-insensitively (src/remote/http.rs:37-43); Request::path drops the query (src/remote/http.rs:33-35). The five assertions at src/remote/http.rs:301-310 match the record exactly. C=2/S=3/F=4 stand; U=2 is right because tests/remote_web.rs:80-110 sends a capitalised Host through the socket, so name normalisation is also covered end to end, while query extraction and the mixed-case X-Test lookup are only asserted here.

Verified all three guards in production: MAX_BODY = 64 KiB (src/remote/http.rs:15), content_length > MAX_BODY bails (src/remote/http.rs:177-179), any transfer-encoding header bails (src/remote/http.rs:180-182) and a line starting with space/tab bails as folded (src/remote/http.rs:157-159). The test cases at src/remote/http.rs:322-330 hit exactly those boundaries. C=3 (framing and memory guards in front of a keystroke/read API), U=3 (no other suite sends oversized/chunked/folded requests), F=4 stand; S=3 is right because each case only asserts is_err, not the error kind or the MAX_BODY boundary itself.

install_terminal_fonts at src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:98-155 returns TerminalFonts::current_monospace (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:34-57) when the home font directory is unavailable or the family is not installed; in that path all four FontIds are the same family and the test only queries one braille glyph (src/bin/ovrcr-gui.rs:158-186).
